Allenones: Asymmetric Allylic Alkylation, Z/E Divergent Allylic
Alkylation, and [5 + 2] Annulation

∥
Yimin Hu,
∥

ABSTRACT: Metal-catalyzed allenylic substitution reactions
where allenes serve as electrophilic precursors have been
recognized as a rapid way for novel allene construction. On the
contrary, the chemistry in which allenes act as nucleophiles has
been far less investigated, especially in a powerful platform such as
metal-catalyzed allylic alkylation reactions. We herein describe two
unprecedented palladium-catalyzed allylic alkylation reactions of an
allene nucleophile. In the first reaction, using vinyloxazolidinones as
the allyl precursor, the palladium-catalyzed asymmetric allylation of
trisubstituted allenones worked well to prepare an array of axially
chiral tetrasubstituted allenes. Mechanistic studies and density
functional theory (DFT) calculations indicated that weak hydro-
gen-bonding interaction between the acidic C(sp
2
)−H of allenone and the nitrogen anion of chiral π-azaallyl-Pd species is key to the
success of stereocontrol. This reaction revealed the intriguing reactivity of nucleophilic allenones in a metal-catalyzed asymmetric
allylation reaction for the first time. In the second reaction, with the use of allenylethylene carbonates as π-oxyallyl-Pd precursors, the
palladium-catalyzed allylic alkylation reaction of allenone presented unique reactivity under different reaction conditions to provide
divergent synthetic access to (E)- and (Z)-allenyl diene products. Interestingly, the subsequent sequential intramolecular
cyclization/isomerization reaction of the (Z)-product delivered dihydrooxepine derivatives as [5 + 2] annulation products.
KEYWORDS: asymmetric catalysis, palladium catalysis, allylation, annulation, chiral allene, axial chirality
■
INTRODUCTION
Allene motifs ubiquitously existed in natural products,
bioactive molecules, and functional materials.
1
Therefore, the
development of catalytic systems that allow the synthesis of
various allenes, especially the challenging multisubstituted
allenes, has attracted a lot of attention from chemical
communities. This research topic has been greatly expanded
during the past two decades, and diverse elegant strategies have
been established for the efficient synthesis of allenes. Among
them, strategies via catalytic functionalization of achiral or
racemic substrates for direct construction of functionalized
allenes in both enantio- and nonenantioselective patterns have
drawn particular interest.
2−4
In this context, the research group
of Ma is listed as one of the main contributors. Various
enantioselective catalytic protocols such as β-elimination,
allenylic and propargylic substitution, Heck reaction, Suzuki
coupling, alkynyl ketimine addition, and allenylation of alkynes
with aldehydes have been developed by the group, allowing
convenient synthesis of structurally diverse functionalized
allenes.
4
Recently, endeavors have been made to prepare
functionalized allenes by using the Pd- or Ir-catalyzed allenylic
substitution protocols, where racemic or achiral allenes served
as electrophiles to couple with diverse nucleophiles.
5
As a
result, a variety of glorious designs including mono- and dual
catalysis have been demonstrated, making this strategy one of
the most straightforward and reliable pathways to access
functionalized allenes in both enantio- and nonenantioselective
patterns (Scheme 1a).
2−5
However, it was usually mandatory
for such a strategy to have specific preinstalled leaving groups
in the allenylic position to form the key π-methyleneallylic
palladium intermediate. This limited the types of both allene
substrates and corresponding allene products to a certain
extent. Thus, developing alternative catalytic protocols that
allow the use of expanded types of allenes would be of great

significance for the diverse synthesis of novel multisubstituted
allene compounds.
In 1993, the Tsuboi group reported an aldol condensation of
nucleophilic allenes with aldehydes, revealing the fascinating
potential of allenes to act as nucleophiles.
6a
In 2009, Miller and
co-workers described the first enantioselective addition of
allenoate to N-acyl imines under the catalysis of a chiral
peptide catalyst.
6b
Within both works, electron-deficient
allenes bearing a C(sp
2
)−H bond activated in situ serve as
precursors for the cumulenolate anion or its equivalent, which
could be trapped by various electrophiles in an enantio- or
nonenantioselective way (Scheme 1b). Indeed, this idea was
further verified soon by later works of Miller,
6c
Maruoka,
7
Feng/Liu,
8
Yu,
9
and List.
10
To date, electrophiles such as
aldehydes, ketones, and aryl and allylic bromides have been
successfully employed via asymmetric Lewis base or acid
catalysis.
6−10
However, the state of the art is still limited to the
previously mentioned several examples. Novel catalytic
coupling processes of the nucleophilic cumulenolate anion
with various types of electrophiles are still in high demand. In
2020, exploiting this cumulenolate anion chemistry, our group
disclosed asymmetric allylic alkylation of allenones and
Morita−Baylis−Hillman carbonates under organocatalysis.
11
Nevertheless, the catalytic method for the coupling of the
cumulenolate anion with widely used π-allyl-Pd intermediates
in either the enantio- or nonenantioselective pattern is still
unknown to date (Scheme 1c).
On the other hand, the direct allylation reactions of the
C(sp
2
)−H bond have attracted broad attention due to the
ubiquitous presence of allyl aromatic rings and allyl olefins in
bioactive molecules.
12
Currently, the direct allylation reactions
of the aromatic C(sp
2
)−H bond have been thoroughly studied
via metal catalysis, organocatalysis, or dual catalysis in both
asymmetric and nonasymmetric patterns.
13,14
In comparison,
the direct allylation of the vinylic C(sp
2
)−H bond, especially in
an enantioselective way, was less investigated because of a lack
of viable activation mode (Scheme 2a). To date, successful
examples of direct allylation of the vinylic C(sp
2
)−H bond
were very rare.
15
In this regard, as mentioned above, we
recently disclosed direct allylation of the allenylic C(sp
2
)−H
bond via organocatalysis.
11
Considering that allylpalladium
intermediates were extremely versatile in asymmetric allylation
reactions of the C(sp
3
)−H bond,
14
we envisioned that the
allylation of the allenylic C(sp
2
)−H bond through palladium
catalysis could be feasible. Our laboratory has been devoted to
developing diverse annulation and allylation reactions with the
use of palladium catalysis, focusing on the development of new
precursors of allylpalladium intermediates.
16
In 2021, we
synthesized allenylethylene carbonates (AECs) as highly
reactive precursors of π-oxyallyl-Pd species, which displayed
good performance in several interesting transformations.
16a
Very recently, we reported a fungicide-inspired precursor of π-
allylpalladium intermediates that underwent [5 + 3] and [3 +
2] cycloadditions as well as allylation reaction.
16e
Combining
our continuous interest in both the allenylic C(sp
2
)−H
nucleophile and the diverse reactivity of the novel precursors
of π-allylpalladium intermediates, we herein present our results
on allylic alkylation reactions of nucleophilic allenones. In the
first part, enantioselective coupling of the allenones with π-
azaallyl-Pd species gave rise to axially chiral allylic allene
products, which represents the first example of the Pd-
catalyzed asymmetric allylation reaction of the allenylic
C(sp
2
)−H nucleophile. In the other part, we realized Pd-
catalyzed Z/E divergent allylic alkylation reactions of

intramolecular cyclization/isomerization reaction of the (Z)-
allylic product (Scheme 2b).

To demonstrate the application potential of this reaction, a
scale-up reaction was conducted (Scheme 5a), affording the
desired product 3aq in 96% yield (538 mg), along with 90% ee
and 7:1 Z/E. The axially chiral allene product 3aq was found
to be highly reactive. It furnished a thermal [3 + 2]
cycloaddition with C,N-cyclic azomethine imine 4 in chloro-
form at 90 °C, delivering chiral hexahydropyrazole[5,1-
a]isoquinoline derivatives 5 in 68% yield with >20:1 dr and
76% ee (Scheme 5b). The accurate structure of product 5 has
been unambiguously confirmed through X-ray crystallographic
analysis.
17

Having proved that the cumulenolate anion generated from
allenone 1 could be well captured by π-azaallyl-Pd species in
Pd-catalyzed allylic alkylation reactions, we became interested
in capturing the cumulenolate anion with alternative allyl-Pd
species from some other precursors such as allenylethylene
carbonates 6 (AECs), which was previously reported by our
group for a Pd-catalyzed [3 + 3] annulation.
16a
As shown in
Scheme 6, the cumulenolate anion generated in situ was readily
captured by the π-oxyallyl-Pd species to give allenyl diene
products (Z)-8 and (E)-8 under different reaction conditions.
Moreover, product (Z)-8 further performed an intramolecular
cyclization/isomerization reaction to form [5 + 2] annulation
product 7. However, as another potential coupling product, the
allene−allene coupling product was not observed in this
reaction.

CONCLUSIONS
In summary, we achieved palladium-catalyzed allenylic C-
(sp
2
)−H allylation reactions for the first time. In the first part,
a series of trisubstituted allenones and 5-vinyloxazolidine-2,4-
diones underwent an asymmetric allylation reaction under mild
reaction conditions to afford various axially chiral tetrasub-
stituted allenones in satisfactory yields with moderate to
excellent stereoselectivity (up to 96% ee and up to 20:1 Z/E).
Mechanistic investigation and DFT calculations indicated that
appropriate hydrogen-bonding interaction between the acidic
C(sp
2
)−H of allene and the nitrogen anion of chiral π-allyl-Pd
species dominated the successful stereocontrol of the allylation
reaction. In the other part, we developed Pd-catalyzed allylic
alkylation of allenones and allenylethylene carbonates,
providing divergent access to (E)- and (Z)-configured allenyl
diene products. Moreover, the subsequent sequential intra-
molecular cyclization/isomerization process enabled a [5 + 2]
annulation reaction to give an array of dihydrooxepine
derivatives. The current reactions described here revealed the
high potential of allenylic nucleophiles to be applied in more
transition metal-catalyzed allylation reactions, which offers
more fascinating opportunities in the synthesis of function-
alized allenes.
